2610.06464.title: A Physics-Guided Transformer Framework for Electromigration Analysis in Multi-Segment Interconnects
2610.06464.paper_summary: As technology scales to smaller nodes, increasing current densities make electromigration (EM) one of the dominant reliability challenges in on-chip interconnects. Accurate transient stress analysis is needed to identify wires susceptible to EM degradation, but applying physics-based solvers across many interconnects remains computationally expensive. This paper proposes a physics-guided transformer framework for fast EM stress prediction in multi-segment interconnect lines. The framework converts each line into geometry- and DC-aware segment tokens and uses transformer attention to capture line-level context. A lightweight query decoder then predicts stress at selected locations and time instants. The model is trained with an objective that combines normalized supervised regression, linewise relative-$L_2$ loss, and physics-guided continuity and terminal-flux terms. Experiments on IBM power grid benchmarks show that the proposed model achieves relative-$L_2$ error below 8\% and reaches up to 2459.68$\times$ speedup compared with the matrix exponential~solver.
2610.06464.paper_summary_zh: 隨著技術縮小到更小的節點，增加的電流密度使得電遷移（EM）成為片上互連中主要的可靠性挑戰之一。準確的瞬態應力分析是識別易受EM降解影響的導線所需，但在許多互連中應用基於物理的求解器仍然計算成本高昂。本文提出了一種物理引導的Transformer框架，用於快速預測多段互連線中的EM應力。該框架將每條線轉換為幾何和直流感知的段令牌，並使用Transformer注意力來捕捉線級上下文。然後，輕量級查詢解碼器在選定的位置和時間點預測應力。該模型的訓練目標結合了標準化的監督回歸、逐行相對-$L_2$損失，以及物理引導的連續性和端點通量項。對IBM電力網基準的實驗表明，所提出的模型實現了低於8\%的相對-$L_2$誤差，並與矩陣指數求解器相比達到了高達2459.68$\times$的加速。
